```{r}
library("tidyverse")
```

In order to reproduce the supplementary figure 1A, we must create normalized data according to the authors descriptions. The purpose of this figure is to check that the two seperate RNA analyses, quantitative reverse transcriptase PCR and RNA sequencing, are compatible, which is required to asses the transcriptome profile of the genotypes in the article.

According to the figure text in the 'Supplementary Table 1' ([link to zip file](https://oup.silverchair-cdn.com/oup/backfile/Content_public/Journal/plcell/26/1/10.1105_tpc.113.119453/4/plcell_v26_1_89_s1.zip?Expires=1797371807&Signature=3BN0htJRMAATym2z08CPcXVMxuYvsSnkZsNURhndtgUOTyH7p~ZMPCHryFMQbh6D0FFbNpCs5IMmSkSP2QfCqHEyo95tK20eQ3Tmqi~ygJ42URncQo9-sN8jWQe9ln-3oojDYRZ0V9dtOSM2rFlfeGwoai15UGklX2UmItm0rpHsBmvIFID2dZPcR2zWWehQG4UB1GfNSSnCGneMn8rGFinTTgQNm9ib0ca9l2DT9Xlvf5t7w7HaHqz9VUncVV4HLdtd5~6X8XutM-7Dwvuny6ESP~BS76sSZnMESOVmwiHiTUKF2blhJOuixLS88IMN-VeSWBNBeNVK6qx00ryGbQ__&Key-Pair-Id=APKAIE5G5CRDK6RD3PGA)), the RPKM (reads per kilobase per million mapped reads) data must all be normalized such that the wild type expression after 45 days of growth (45 DAP or "P age") is equal to 1.

#### Creating relative expression data from the qRT-PCR experiment

As we are going to be working with this data separately in an analysis, we are going to create a new tibble, with the standardized columns, as opposed to adding it to the already cleaned data set.

```{r}
#| label: Loading packages
#| message: false

library("tidyverse")
library("readxl")
```

#### Load data

```{r}
#| label: Load dataset
#| message: false

Data_set_1_clean <- read_rds("../data/02_df1_clean.rds")
head(Data_set_1_clean)
```

```{r}
Data_set_1_sf1 <- Data_set_1_clean |> 
  select(3:14,24) |>       #select the RPKM data
  relocate(Gene_Name) |>   #moves gene name column to be the first
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Gene_Name,     #only gene name is to be kept the same, remaining are pivoted
    #.value names the columns mean and sd, and keeps the numerical value of each row
    names_to = c("Dataset", "Age", ".value"), 
    names_sep = "_"
  ) |> 
  #converts <chr> to <dbl> and removes ',' as thousands delimiter
  mutate(across(c(mean, sd), parse_number)) |>  
  group_by(Gene_Name) |>
  mutate(
   ref       = mean[Dataset == "AC" & Age == "P"],
   mean_norm = mean / ref,
   sd_norm   = sd / ref
  ) |> 
  ungroup()


Data_set_1_sf1
```

#### Save the workable files in data/ folder

```{r}
# use rds to save data types 
write_rds(Data_set_1_sf1, file = "../data/03_sf1_aug.rds")
```

#### Example graph

```{r}
gene_id <- "GRAS"

Data_set_1_sf1 |> 
  filter(Gene_Name == gene_id) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Age,
             y = mean_norm,
             fill = Dataset)) + 
    
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.8) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#4f81bd",
                               "#c0504d",
                               "#9bbb59")) +
  
  geom_linerange(
    aes(ymin = mean_norm, ymax = mean_norm + sd_norm),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    size = 0.8
  ) +
  # cap at the top only (ymin = ymax, so no vertical part is drawn)
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean_norm + sd_norm, ymax = mean_norm + sd_norm),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.25,
    size = 0.8) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 2.5),
    breaks = 0:4,
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) + 
  
  labs(title = bquote(bolditalic(.(gene_id)))) + 
  
  theme_bw() + 
  
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "bottom", 
        legend.title=element_blank(),
        legend.background = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = "white", linewidth = 0.4), 
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "black"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "black"),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "gray", linewidth = 0.5),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = "gray", fill=NA, linewidth=1.5)) 
  
```

#### Creating relative expression data from the RNA-seq experiment

```{r}
Data_set_1_sf2 <- Data_set_1_clean |> 
  select(15:24) |>       #select the FC data
  relocate(Gene_Name) |> 
  rename(                # Creating names that are easier to read
    AC_PG     = `FC_AC(P/G)`, 
    TF18_P_AC = `FC_TF18_P/AC_P`, 
    rin_P_AC  = `FC_rin_P/AC_P`, 
    TF18_G_AC = `FC_TF18_G/AC_G`,
    rin_G_AC  = `FC_rin_G/AC_G`
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    AC_P   = 1,
    rin_P  = 2^rin_P_AC,
    TF18_P = 2^TF18_P_AC,
    AC_G   = 2^(-AC_PG),
    rin_G  = 2^(rin_G_AC  - AC_PG),
    TF18_G = 2^(TF18_G_AC - AC_PG)
  ) |> 
  select(Gene_Name, AC_G, AC_P, rin_G, rin_P, TF18_G, TF18_P) |> 
  filter(Gene_Name %in% c("RIN","TDR4","FUL2","ACS2","ACS4","PSY1","PG2A","CNR","GRAS")) |> #missing GRAS
  pivot_longer(-Gene_Name,
               names_to = c("Genotype", "Age"),
               names_sep = "_",
               values_to = "RNA_seq_FC")

Data_set_1_sf2
```
